2a, 2, and some 3a are soft armor- think kevlar. Some 3a, all 3 and 4 are Hard armor. The industry also added a rating of 3+ to cover common rifle threats not covered by 3, such as very fast 5.56 (xm193) or steel core penetrators (green tips)

Soft armor is chiefly for pistol calibers, hard armor is for rifle calibers.

Soft armor is significantly lighter than hard armor, so most of the time, police will be wearing a soft vest, unless the situation warrants it (I sure hope they're wearing hard armor when they confront those BLM faggots...). These can defeat most common 'pistol' calibers (380, 9mm, 45 etc) but it gets fuzzy. The type of bullet (JHP- Jacketed Hollow point) FMJ (Full metal jacket) can make a difference- Hollow points are designed to transfer energy to target by mushrooming out thereby increasing the surface area and hence tissue damage on unarmored opponents. Because of this, they are significantly less effective against armor.

The type of ammunition and the barrel length both affect penetration. Speed defeats armor (except ceramic, in which case it's speed and mass, or multiple hits). The longer the barrel (with diminishing returns) the faster the bullet. So if you put a plus p (higher than normal pressure, hence greater speeds/energy) 9mm round in a carbine with an 11 in barrel it may have enough speed to defeat armor that is generally rated to withstand 9mm. (these ratings are also speed dependent).

It sounds more complex than it is. Just remember different armor is rated for different bullet mass/hardness/speed.
